# Model 12 (SVR)

An attempt at using support vector machines. Interestingly this turned out to be the worst performing model.

```{python}
#| warning: false

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.svm import SVR
from sklearn.metrics import root_mean_squared_error

# Read data
data = pd.read_csv('../PACFiles/analysis_data.csv')

X_raw = pd.get_dummies(data.drop(['customer_id', 'monthly_spend'], axis = 1), drop_first=True).fillna(0)
y = data['monthly_spend']
X_train_raw, X_test_raw, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X_raw, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=617)
scale = StandardScaler()
scale.fit(X_train_raw)
X_train = scale.transform(X_train_raw)
X_test = scale.transform(X_test_raw)

model = SVR(kernel = 'rbf', C = 1, gamma=0.1) 
model.fit(X_train, y_train)

scoring_data = pd.read_csv('../PACFiles/scoring_data.csv')
scoring_X_raw = pd.get_dummies(scoring_data.drop(['customer_id'], axis=1), drop_first=True).fillna(0)

scoring_X_raw = scoring_X_raw.reindex(columns=X_raw.columns, fill_value=0)
scoring_X_scaled = scale.transform(scoring_X_raw)

final_predictions = model.predict(scoring_X_scaled)

# Construct submission
submission_file = pd.DataFrame({'customer_id': scoring_data.customer_id, 'monthly_spend': final_predictions})
submission_file.to_csv('../PACFiles/submission_file_13.csv', index=False)

pred_train = model.predict(X_train)
pred_test = model.predict(X_test)
rmse_train = root_mean_squared_error(y_train, pred_train)
rmse_test = root_mean_squared_error(y_test, pred_test)
print("Training RMSE:", rmse_train)
print("Testing RMSE:", rmse_test)
```
